name: Savoy Palace
description: John of Gaunt's London residence on the Strand, reputed the grandest private house in England. Systematically destroyed by the rebels on 13 June 1381 -- goods burned or thrown into the Thames rather than stolen, a distinction chroniclers (Henry Knighton) record explicitly, framing it as punishment of Gaunt rather than plunder. Contemporary estimates of the destroyed contents' value run to roughly £10,000.
